page.overview:
Who is Acanthopholis?

(meaning “spiny scales”) is an extinct genus of Nodosauridae dinosaur that lived in England during the Late Cretaceous period. The armor of Acanthopholis consisted of oval keeled plates set almost horizontally into the skin, with long spikes protruding from the neck and shoulder area, along the spine. Named by Thomas Huxley in 1867, one of the most prominent scientists and thinkers of 19th century Europe, Acanthopholis has had a somewhat controversial history. It was probably slightly smaller and lighter than its North American nodosaur relatives.

Acanthopholis was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.
